zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開盤固定收益主論點

油價再度大跌，降低伊朗衝突所帶來的通膨溢價，也促使交易員下修未來一年對聯準會升息幅度的預期，美國公債因而在8月4日延續漲勢。2年期殖利率下跌4.5個基點至4.193%，5年期下跌6.2個基點至4.326%，10年期下跌6.3個基點至4.615%，30年期則下跌5.3個基點至5.176%。美國、伊朗與區域調停方出現朝荷莫茲海峽臨時安排取得進展的跡象，但恢復正常航運所需的條款尚未談妥，也尚未落實。

WTI原油下跌6.41%至每桶$75.19，創7月10日以來最低收盤價；布蘭特原油下跌5.96%至$78.78。卡達表示提案草案已經擬妥，美國財政部長Scott Bessent則稱協議可能在一天內達成。伊朗也在考慮允許歐洲國家協助清除荷莫茲海峽的水雷，這有別於先前公開堅持排雷工作必須完全由伊朗掌控的立場。即使停火能否持久、安全保證與水道控制權仍未解決，主要石油與液化天然氣航道可能恢復通行，已足以推動市場進一步重估能源風險。

美國公債漲勢同時來自實質利率與通膨補償下降。10年期實質殖利率下跌2.8個基點至2.387%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下跌3.5個基點至2.228%。這項拆解顯示，外交消息既降低能源對物價的預期推力，也壓低投資人持有存續期部位所要求的實質報酬。殖利率曲線小幅趨平，2年與10年期利差收窄1.8個基點至42.2個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄0.8個基點至98.3個基點。

這並不是一場逃離成長風險的交易。S&P 500上漲1.79%並創新高，Nasdaq 100上漲3.32%，費城半導體指數更大漲6.55%。美國6月職缺降幅超出預期，但招聘略為增加，解僱情況變化不大，顯示勞動需求僅邊際轉弱，並未突然受創。這樣的組合讓投資人降低聯準會多次升息的機率，卻沒有開始定價經濟即將萎縮。

不過，債市的修復仍不完整。10年期殖利率仍比一個月前高13個基點，30年期則高19個基點，通膨不確定性、聯準會溝通及未來美國公債供給所形成的較長期溢價依舊存在。費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson也凸顯了這項區別。她支持上週維持利率不變的決定，並認為政策略具限制性；但她表示，若基礎通膨無法繼續改善，本身就會成為需要進一步收緊政策的證據。

## 油價紓壓同時傳導至實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率

週二原油下跌，使原本試探性的外交表態轉化為美國公債連續第2天上漲。在與債市走勢對應的盤中統計中，WTI下跌5.7%，紐約時段收盤跌逾6%；布蘭特原油則收在$80以下。自美國2月底攻擊伊朗以來，荷莫茲海峽航運受阻不斷改變整體通膨、生產成本及央行政策的預期路徑，美國公債殖利率也一再隨油價波動。

最新提案著重於重新開放海峽，而不是全面解決美國與伊朗的衝突。卡達表示臨時方案已經傳閱，Bessent與卡達代表都對即將達成協議表達期待。外交人士指出，德黑蘭私下已軟化反對歐洲參與排雷的立場；若能成行，船東與保險公司將可透過獨立管道評估航道是否安全。

若要部署歐洲海軍行動，仍須取得伊朗的安全保證、能夠維持的停火，以及伊斯蘭革命衛隊同意。該組織曾主導對船舶的攻擊，成員對外國介入仍意見分歧。伊朗持續要求掌控海峽並收取通行費，美國則反對這項安排。與阿曼的談判聚焦於一條據信布有水雷的新航道，因此即使各方同意展開協商，後續仍須實際排雷並建立可信的安全架構。

這些限制之所以重要，是因為週二的市場走勢反映的是航運再度受阻機率下降，而不是交通已經恢復。可觀察到的船舶通行量仍極為有限，歷時五個月的衝突也使仰賴進口的經濟體持續面臨燃料與電力短缺。儘管如此，市場認為伊朗立場改變比再一次籠統表達談判意願更具實質意義，因為讓外部力量參與排雷，將直接處理阻礙商業航運恢復的一項現實障礙。

利率反應遍及各天期，但以曲線中段與10年期最為明顯。5年期與10年期殖利率均下跌逾6個基點，相較之下，2年期下跌4.5個基點，30年期下跌5.3個基點。這使曲線小幅趨平，而非再度呈現多頭陡峭化，反映投資人移除部分中期通膨與政策緊縮溢價，同時仍為財政供給及能源衝擊可能留下長期影響保留可觀的長端溢價。

10年期損益兩平通膨率的跌幅，占同天期名目殖利率變動略多於一半。10年期損益兩平通膨率收在2.228%，單日下跌3.5個基點，較一個月前低1.1個基點。相較之下，即使週二回落，10年期實質殖利率仍比一個月前高14.1個基點。因此，能源壓力緩解對近期通膨補償升幅的逆轉程度，高於對實質折現率升幅的逆轉。

隨漲勢發展，美國公債交易活動也隨之增加。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.166兆，較前一個交易日增加5.4%，總計388,074筆。名目付息債券交易量增加8.2%至$9,250億；逾7年至10年期券種增加15.9%至$1,656億，逾3年至5年期券種則增加10.4%至$2,390億。這些數據無法判斷投資人的買賣方向，但顯示殖利率跌幅最大的區段伴隨現券市場參與升高，而不是成交異常清淡。

長天期債券指數的反彈幅度也高於前端。ICE美國政府債券20年以上指數上漲0.78%，7至10年期指數上漲0.46%，1至3年期指數僅上漲0.11%。即使單日走高，20年以上指數在一個月內仍下跌2.81%。這與殖利率曲線呈現的訊息一致：油價下跌帶來實質紓壓，卻未能消除先前實質殖利率上升與長天期利率風險累積的成本。

風險性資產把油價下跌視為供給衝擊緩解。半導體指數上漲6.55%，領漲科技股；S&P 500與道瓊工業指數均創新高。投資等級債與高收益債基金同樣上揚，LQD上漲0.61%，HYG上漲0.30%。美元指數下跌0.09%。黃金期貨則上漲2.33%至$4,127.80，顯示即期能源溢價雖然下降，市場對通膨或地緣政治避險工具的需求仍在。

## Paulson仍以通膨進展作為聯準會政策檢驗

Paulson提出當天最清楚的新論述，說明聯準會面臨的政策選擇。這位今年擁有貨幣政策投票權的費城聯準銀行總裁表示，對她而言，上週維持利率不變並不是一項難以抉擇的決定。她認為當前政策立場略具限制性，但這只是暫時判斷，並不等於主張長期按兵不動。

她提出兩種情境。第一種是通膨數據持續改善、通膨預期維持穩定，證明現行利率能在可接受的時間內讓通膨回到2%。另一種情境則是，過去一年基礎通膨僅小幅下降，顯示政策限制程度仍然不足。在後一種情況下，若時間經過而通膨沒有進一步改善，就會成為收緊政策的證據，而不是繼續等待的理由。

這項區別相當重要，因為Paulson估計基礎通膨仍在2.4%至2.8%，高於聯準會目標。她肯定6月個人消費支出物價指數有所改善，但形容這僅是其中一步。她願意保持耐心的條件，是剔除波動較大食品與能源價格後的指標持續進步，而不是只有原油再度下跌。她也指出，勞動市場穩定、中東局勢造成的物價不確定性，以及AI基礎設施投資，都可能讓需求與部分價格保持堅挺。

6月職缺數據只帶來有限紓壓。職缺由5月的754萬降至736萬，降幅超出預期，醫療保健、休閒與餐旅、批發貿易及商業服務業均見減少；運輸與倉儲業職缺增加，聯邦政府職缺則升至2024年底以來最高。招聘略為增加，解僱變化不大。因此，數據顯示職缺有所降溫，卻未反映整體就業流動廣泛惡化。

美國貿易報告也提供跨境需求放緩的證據，但不足以證明國內經濟陷入下行。6月商品與服務貿易逆差縮小5.6%至$733億。進口下跌1.8%，為年初以來首次下降；出口減少0.9%。整季貿易數據波動較大，原因是關稅、伊朗衝突與AI相關投資改變了採購時點和組成。

短期利率市場主要反映油價下跌，而非勞動展望突然轉弱。期貨定價顯示，9月會議約有15個基點的升息幅度，超過升息1碼的一半，年底前則完整反映一次升息。就在前一週，市場還完整反映兩次升息。能源價格下降降低了連續升息的急迫性，但Paulson提出的條件與依然穩定的勞動市場，使一次升息仍留在市場定價情境中。

美國公債殖利率曲線也支持這項解讀。2年期殖利率降至7月20日以來最低，但4.5個基點的跌幅仍小於5年與10年期。若投資人已認定勞動需求正在急遽崩解，通常應由曲線前端主導漲勢。實際上，市場只是降低預期升息幅度，並從中期券種移除部分通膨補償，同時保留聯準會今年稍後仍可能採取行動的可能性。

供給則是另一項獨立牽制。美國財政部將於8月5日華盛頓時間上午8時30分公布8月至10月的中期公債與長債標售計畫。自2024年5月以來，官員一直表示，名目付息債與浮動利率債券的標售規模至少未來幾季可能保持不變。交易商普遍預期即將發布的公告將延續這項立場，但到期債務與持續性的赤字，可能迫使財政部明年擴大固定利率借款計畫。

市場對最終擴大標售的時點仍有分歧。交易商最常見的預估已由2027年2月延後至5月，部分預測更指向8月。CIBC、德意志銀行、摩根士丹利與富國銀行預期，財政部至少會刪除「至少」一詞，使措辭轉趨保留。摩根大通策略師則認為這樣調整合乎情理，但財政部可能為避免推升長期殖利率而不作更動。關鍵差別在於，一方面維持目前標售規模穩定，另一方面則開始讓投資人為穩定期結束的時點預作準備。

因此，週二漲勢降低了政策與供給溢價中的能源成分，卻沒有解決這兩項問題。油價可以迅速改變近期通膨的機率分布，但Paulson的決策準則仍取決於基礎通膨；30年期券種面對的借款展望，也遠超出當前這一輪外交進展。這正是長債雖然上漲，殖利率仍高於5.17%，且單月升幅遠大於2年期公債的原因。

## 初級信貸市場獎勵清楚交易、拒絕薄弱條款

美國投資等級初級市場對不屬於AI借款週期的收購融資展現強勁需求。AbbVie發行$100億債券，協助支應尚待完成的Apogee Therapeutics收購案，最高訂單約達$630億。這略高於Amazon上月發行$250億債券所收到的需求，也遠高於AbbVie今年2月發行$80億債券時約$390億的最高訂單。

AbbVie原先計畫募集至少$80億，最終完成分為9個券次、年期橫跨2年至40年的交易。最長天期債券的定價為美國公債殖利率加92個基點，較初步討論水準收窄約33個基點。這顯示當發行人、資金用途及交易結構清楚時，投資人願意承接更長天期的債券。

募集資金將協助支應AbbVie擬以$109億收購Apogee的交易，預計本季完成。隨著Skyrizi面臨的競爭升高，這項收購旨在強化AbbVie的抗發炎藥物產品組合。該公司先前公布的第2季業績也優於預期，受惠於免疫學、神經科學業務及Botox銷售復甦。

AbbVie是週二6家投資等級借款人之一，這些發行人合計籌得$173億，其中包括Skyworks Solutions的收購融資。市場反應顯示，投資人將傳統企業融資與近期對資料中心及AI債務的疲態區別看待。Amazon發行$250億債券後，AI相關債券走弱；7月一筆涉及BlackRock的資料中心融資，初期需求也偏軟。AbbVie的借款需求小得多，收購理由又與AI無關，因此相對於發行規模，其訂單簿更為充足。

槓桿貸款市場則呈現相反結果。Baker Tilly撤回一筆約$30億的貸款，原本計畫用於再融資私募信貸債務並發放股利。部分潛在買方要求的利差，高於這家會計師事務所及其股東Hellman & Friedman與Valeas Capital Partners願意提供的水準。Baker Tilly表示，公司曾評估這項機會型再融資，待市場條件更有利時可能再次進場。

擬議股利最高可能達$10億，若完成，將成為今年規模最大的非投資等級股利交易。對於原已在評估利率長期維持高檔，以及低評等企業到期債務繁重的債權人而言，這項資金用途進一步削弱了交易吸引力。撤案表明，即使流動性充裕，投資人仍會抗拒把再融資與大額贊助股東現金提取綁在一起的交易。

這項對比並不只是投資等級與槓桿融資之間的差異，而是市場即使仍能吸收大型交易，投資人也會區分不同借款人與結構。AbbVie不僅把發行規模由原先設定的最低水準向上調整，定價也大幅收窄；Baker Tilly面對貸款人要求就槓桿與股利提取獲得更多補償，最終無法完成規模相近的再融資。

次級市場研究顯示，高評等與垃圾級債券的界線也普遍受到侵蝕。納入美元與歐元投資等級指數、合計約$1,000億的債券，其交易利差已高於雙B級利差曲線。Oracle與Stellantis都是債券定價逼近垃圾債市場的大型發行人；ICE BofA一項追蹤已由投資等級遭降評公司債券的指數，也升至2024年初以來最高。

壓力來自多個方向。Oracle在資料中心的支出，使其成為市場憂慮舉債投資AI的焦點；不過，該公司利差7月一度突破雙B級水準後，到8月初已重新收窄至該水準以下。Stellantis則面臨中國業者競爭，股價也大幅下跌。商業發展公司與私募信貸業者同樣受到檢視，因為它們曝險於可能遭AI顛覆的軟體公司。

債券以類似垃圾級的利差交易，並不保證發行人一定會遭降評。市場重新定價的速度往往快於信評機構，利差也可能在評等改變前回復。Fitch表示，其分析著重於營收成長、利潤率、現金流生成能力及跨週期的前瞻槓桿。不過，近期跨越雙B級曲線的投資等級債券規模異常龐大，仍顯示較高融資成本與科技顛覆的影響，已不再局限於明確屬於投機級的借款人。

在這樣的背景下，週二初級市場的結果更具訊息意義。信貸市場依然開放，但交易能否完成，愈來愈取決於投資人是否因特定資金用途與信用惡化風險而獲得充分補償。高評等製藥公司為已宣布的收購案籌資，能吸引超過發行規模6倍的訂單；由贊助股東持有、同時尋求再融資與股利發放的公司，則無法以偏好的利差完成交易。

## 全球政策分歧遭遇能源驅動的成長衝擊

投資人比較美國、英國與日本的政策可信度、財政風險和通膨曝險後，對主權債券的需求正轉向歐洲。UBS Asset Management與Guinness Global Investors持續買進德國公債；Barings減持美國公債，轉而增持義大利、西班牙與法國債券；Aviva Investors則認為歐元區部位具吸引力。即使伊朗衝突已推升能源成本，這些機構共同的論點仍是，歐洲成長較弱、貨幣政策架構也較可預測，能提供相對穩定性。

不過，市場定價仍反映ECB有相當大的升息空間。交換市場顯示今年將升息1碼，且再升息一次的機率超過60%；相較之下，一筆Euribor選擇權交易押注年底前僅升息12.5個基點，遠低於交換市場反映的約41個基點。爭議不在於能源衝擊是否重要，而是在德國10年期公債殖利率升破3%後，市場是否已對衝擊的持續程度定價過多。

歐洲的吸引力仍受到各國財政差異限制。9月預算協商在即，加上總理Giorgia Meloni執政聯盟內部存在政治緊張，投資人對較長天期義大利公債依然審慎。法國10年期公債殖利率比德國公債高近80個基點，在利差補償與政治風險之間形成另一種權衡。英國市場則持續關注10月28日預算案，以及軍事投資與成人社會照護的融資方式；英國30年期公債殖利率已是已開發市場最高。

日本的貨幣政策與市場壓力組合更不穩定。在殖利率維持於數十年高點附近之際，10年期日本政府公債標售需求降至2025年5月以來最弱。日圓下跌0.3%，至約157.70兌1美元，回吐部分美日聯手干預帶來的升幅。日圓仍弱於155；策略師認為，這是判斷官方行動能否持久扭轉貶值趨勢的重要關卡。

若日本再次干預需要美元，仍有出售美國公債以外的選擇。花旗指出，可利用聯準會的外國及國際貨幣當局附買回機制、約$1,600億存放在外國央行的存款，以及歐元資產籌措資金。日本持有超過$1.1兆美國公債，財務大臣片山皋月表示，日本未來將使用聯準會這項機制。這些選項降低匯率防衛自動引發美債拋售的即期風險，但無法解決日圓疲弱背後的利率差距。

美國固定收益市場收盤後公布的日本薪資數據，強化日本央行未來幾個月再次升息的理由。6月名目薪資年增3.4%，高於修正後的5月增幅3.3%；薪資增幅連續五個月超過3%，為34年來最長。基本薪資也成長3.4%；全職勞工剔除獎金、加班費及抽樣扭曲後的指標上升2.9%。實質薪資則連續第六個月成長，增幅為1.7%。

在這批數據之前，企業獲利已連續六季較上年同期成長；由日本勞動組合總連合會代表的勞工，年度薪資協商漲幅也連續第三年超過5%。這些結果支持日本央行的看法，即勞動市場緊俏足以維持薪資成長，儘管食品通膨與生活成本仍對家庭構成壓力。數據公布時間太晚，無法解釋週二美債收盤走勢，卻加深亞洲交易時段面對的政策分歧：油價下跌促使美國市場下修升息預期，日本國內數據則提高日本央行提早行動的可能性。

其他央行仍在因應累積的能源衝擊。馬達加斯加認定貨幣條件已不再具有足夠限制性，將政策利率由12%調升至12.5%，為逾一年來首次升息。央行也把年底通膨預測由9.3%上調至10.1%，並表示升息旨在抑制預期物價漲勢，讓通膨預期朝5%的中期目標靠攏。

在開發中亞洲與太平洋地區，傷害已不只反映於通膨數據。亞洲開發銀行把該地區2026年成長預測由5.1%下調至4.9%，通膨預測則由3.6%上調至4.3%。衛星觀測顯示，自衝突爆發以來，區域內近60%的陸地面積夜間燈光減弱；仰賴進口的孟加拉、巴基斯坦與柬埔寨受創尤其嚴重。燃料短缺與成本上升已干擾製造、運輸及觀光業，亞銀並警告，即使油價回落，債務累積、裁員與投資下降仍可能延續。

歐洲面臨的是另一種供給限制。萊茵河考布河段水位降至21公分，創歷史最低，並預估將在週六降至17公分。駁船正減少載重，運費上升，低水位也限制法國部分核能發電。根據一項估算，這可能使德國全年經濟成長減少0.3個百分點。這項發展使歐洲通膨前景並非全然溫和：經濟活動轉弱有利債券，但運輸與電力供應受阻也可能推高近期成本。

ECB研究發現，伊朗戰爭爆發後，歐元區家庭削減非必要支出的主要原因是前景不確定，而不只是預算受限。名目能源支出增加，住房與食品支出仍具韌性，所得較高家庭的支出減幅最大。這種模式顯示，即使能源成本尚未完全反映在家庭資產負債表上，不確定情緒也能先行削弱需求。

## 前瞻市場意涵

8月5日公布的美國財政部再融資計畫，是最迫切的美國利率風險事件。市場普遍預期8月至10月當季的付息債標售規模維持不變。真正影響市場的問題，是官員會否保留名目付息債與浮動利率票券規模在「至少」未來幾季保持穩定的承諾，或軟化措辭，讓投資人為2027年擴大發行預作準備。刪除這個詞不會增加本季標售規模，卻可能使長端市場提早反映供給轉折。

印度央行同樣將於8月5日作出決策。受訪的30位經濟學家中，有29位預期附買回利率維持在5.25%，僅一位預測升息1碼。6月通膨加速至4.38%，17個月來首次高於印度央行4%的目標；財政部也警告物價壓力正從食品向外擴散。多數經濟學家預期，印度央行將維持本財政年度通膨率5.1%及經濟成長6.6%的預測，但近期油價下跌，提供下修通膨預估的空間。

相較於市場廣泛預期的按兵不動，總裁Sanjay Malhotra提出未來升息的條件更為重要。利率交換反映75至100個基點的升息幅度，其中大部分延後至明年；許多經濟學家則預期10月開始升息。自當局放寬外幣存款與海外借款規定後，已有超過$400億資金流入印度，為流動性與盧比提供支撐。印度央行必須決定要把多少流入資金吸收到外匯存底，同時判斷能源成本是否正在傳導至消費者物價。

週五的美國就業報告將決定職缺下降是否代表勞動市場出現實質降溫。目前預期非農就業人口增加85,000人，高於6月的57,000人，失業率則為4.2%。若數據較強，將支持Paulson的擔憂：如果基礎通膨停滯，略具限制性的政策可能仍不夠。若數據較弱，尤其原油維持在週二的較低水準附近，市場將更進一步下修聯準會升息預期。

荷莫茲海峽仍是變化較快的檢驗。提案草案已經擬妥，伊朗也願意考慮由歐洲參與排雷，因此油價在船舶恢復正常通行前就已下跌。下一階段需要看到的證據，包括可持續的停火、伊朗提供安全保證、伊斯蘭革命衛隊同意，以及實際取得排雷准入。若這些步驟達成，能源再度推高損益兩平通膨率並迫使央行提前緊縮的機率將下降。若各方在控制權、通行費或外國海軍參與問題上意見破裂，則會凸顯兩天債市漲勢有多少是建立在一項尚未完備的安排上。

日本薪資報告把亞洲政策焦點轉向日本央行下一次行動的時點。名目薪資增幅持續高於3%、實質薪資連續六個月成長，加上企業獲利穩健，都強化12月前升息的理由，9月也仍在考慮範圍。日圓能否在不再度干預的情況下遠離近期低點，將決定決策者認為採取行動有多急迫。若日圓再度貶值，不僅會檢驗日本的資金籌措選項，也會考驗美國防止匯率防衛蔓延為美債拋售的努力。

信貸投資人將持續區分能否取得資金與交易條件是否可接受。AbbVie取得$630億訂單，顯示大型收購融資能在定價大幅收窄後順利完成；Baker Tilly撤案則揭示，市場對與贊助股東股利綁定的槓桿再融資需求有限。隨著潛在墮落天使債規模及槓桿債務到期量增加，下一批交易將顯示這項分歧究竟仍只針對個別發行人，還是會成為更廣泛的限制。

overall_summary.headline: 荷莫茲外交進展壓低油價與通膨預期，美國公債延續漲勢
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷莫茲海峽臨時安排出現進展跡象，推動WTI原油下跌6.41%至$75.19、布蘭特原油下跌5.96%至$78.78，美國公債因而連續第二個交易日走高。2年期殖利率下跌4.5個基點至4.193%，5年期下跌6.2個基點至4.326%，10年期下跌6.3個基點至4.615%，30年期則下跌5.3個基點至5.176%。

漲勢同時反映通膨補償與實質利率下降：10年期損益兩平通膨率下跌3.5個基點至2.228%，10年期實質殖利率下跌2.8個基點至2.387%。隨能源風險降低，投資人下修聯準會預期升息幅度；但股市強勁、勞動市場僅溫和降溫，加上Anna Paulson對基礎通膨停滯的警告，使市場仍完整反映年底前升息一次。

紓壓仍有條件，因為正常航運尚未恢復，持久停火、伊朗安全保證、伊斯蘭革命衛隊同意及排雷准入等問題都未解決。較長天期殖利率也仍高於一個月前，顯示當前外交進展以外的供給與通膨溢價依然存在。信貸市場同樣凸顯條款的重要性：AbbVie的收購融資需求旺盛，Baker Tilly則撤回與大額贊助股東股利綁定的槓桿再融資。
overall_summary.summary: 荷莫茲臨時安排出現進展，帶動原油重挫及各天期美國公債殖利率下跌；通膨補償與實質殖利率同步下降，但風險性資產仍具韌性，Paulson也維持對基礎通膨的檢驗，因此聯準會日後升息的可能性仍在。

section_summaries.market_read: 市場下修聯準會預期升息幅度，但未開始定價經濟即將萎縮。
section_summaries.summary: 原油下跌延續美國公債漲勢，荷莫茲臨時安排取得進展，促使通膨補償與實質殖利率下降，殖利率曲線也小幅趨平。這是能源衝擊緩解，而不是逃離成長風險：股市創新高，勞動需求僅邊際轉弱，較長天期殖利率也仍較一個月前明顯偏高。

section_summaries.market_read: 能源壓力緩解對先前通膨補償升幅的逆轉程度，高於對實質折現率升幅的逆轉。
section_summaries.section_title: 油價紓壓同時傳導至實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率
section_summaries.summary: 伊朗願意考慮由歐洲參與排雷，使最新荷莫茲提案比先前籠統表達談判意願更具可行性，帶動WTI下跌逾6%，美國公債則以5年與10年期殖利率跌幅最大。然而，實際航運仍極為有限；若要重新開放海峽，仍須達成持久停火、取得安全保證與伊斯蘭革命衛隊同意，並實際清除水雷。

section_summaries.market_read: 曲線中段領漲反映通膨與政策緊縮壓力降低，並非市場認定勞動需求正在急遽崩解。
section_summaries.section_title: Paulson仍以通膨進展作為聯準會政策檢驗
section_summaries.summary: Anna Paulson支持聯準會維持利率不變，並認為政策略具限制性，但她表示基礎通膨若停止改善，就會成為需要進一步收緊政策的證據。職缺減少尚未構成就業流動廣泛惡化，期貨因此不再完整反映2026年第2次升息，但仍保留年底前升息一次。即將公布的美國財政部再融資計畫，也使供給風險與近期油價重新定價維持分立。

section_summaries.market_read: 投資人流動性支持用途清楚的收購融資，卻不足以消除市場對槓桿與股利提取的抗拒。
section_summaries.section_title: 初級信貸市場獎勵清楚交易、拒絕薄弱條款
section_summaries.summary: AbbVie為收購Apogee籌得$100億，最高訂單約達$630億，不僅擴大發行規模，40年期債券定價也較初步討論水準收窄約33個基點。相較之下，Baker Tilly在貸款人要求更寬利差後，撤回與最高$10億贊助股東股利相關的約$30億再融資。信貸資金仍然可得，但補償、結構與信用惡化風險決定交易能否完成。

section_summaries.market_read: 經濟活動轉弱有利債券，但能源、運輸與財政限制，使各地通膨與期限溢價走勢仍不一致。
section_summaries.section_title: 全球政策分歧遭遇能源驅動的成長衝擊
section_summaries.summary: 投資人權衡較弱成長與較穩定政策，以及財政和能源風險後，歐洲主權債券獲得相對需求；日本公債標售疲弱、日圓再度貶值，則凸顯當地政策組合較不穩定。在亞洲開發中經濟體，能源衝擊促使區域成長預測下修、通膨預測上調；萊茵河水位創新低，也威脅歐洲運輸、電力供應與德國經濟活動。
眼前的關鍵檢驗是美國財政部8月5日再融資計畫的措辭、週五美國就業報告，以及荷莫茲外交能否落實可執行的安全與排雷步驟。這些事件將共同決定債市漲勢能否超越油價風險下降，或仍容易受到供給、通膨及聯準會壓力再起的衝擊。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their rally on Aug. 4 as another sharp fall in oil reduced the inflation premium attached to the Iran conflict and led traders to pare the amount of Federal Reserve tightening expected over the coming year. The 2-year yield fell 4.5 basis points to 4.193%, the 5-year declined 6.2 basis points to 4.326%, the 10-year dropped 6.3 basis points to 4.615% and the 30-year eased 5.3 basis points to 5.176%. The move followed signs that the US, Iran and regional mediators were making progress toward an interim arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz, although the terms needed to restore normal shipping had not been agreed or implemented.

WTI crude fell 6.41% to $75.19, its lowest settlement since July 10, while Brent dropped 5.96% to $78.78. Qatar said a proposal had been drafted, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested an agreement could come within a day. Iran was also considering allowing European countries to help clear mines from Hormuz, a change from its public insistence that demining remain exclusively under Iranian control. The possibility of restoring a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas route was enough to extend the repricing of energy risk, even though ceasefire durability, security assurances and control of the waterway remained unresolved.

The Treasury rally was divided between lower real rates and lower inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield declined 2.8 basis points to 2.387%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 3.5 basis points to 2.228%. That decomposition showed the diplomatic news easing both the expected price impulse from energy and the inflation-adjusted rate investors required to own duration. The curve flattened modestly: 2s10s narrowed 1.8 basis points to 42.2 basis points and 2s30s contracted 0.8 basis point to 98.3 basis points.

The session did not resemble a flight from growth. The S&P 500 rose 1.79% to a record, the Nasdaq 100 gained 3.32% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surged 6.55%. US job openings declined more than expected in June, but hiring picked up slightly and dismissals were little changed, leaving labor demand softer at the margin rather than abruptly impaired. The combination allowed investors to reduce the probability of multiple Fed increases without pricing an imminent contraction.

The recovery in bonds nevertheless remained incomplete. The 10-year yield was still 13 basis points higher than a month earlier and the 30-year was 19 basis points higher, preserving the longer-run premium associated with inflation uncertainty, Fed communication and eventual Treasury supply. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson reinforced that distinction. She supported last week’s decision to hold rates and described policy as mildly restrictive, but said a failure of underlying inflation to make further progress would itself become evidence that more restraint was required.

## Oil Relief Reaches Both Real Yields and Breakevens

Tuesday’s crude decline turned tentative diplomatic language into a second consecutive day of Treasury gains. WTI fell 5.7% in the intraday account associated with the bond move and finished the New York session down more than 6%, while Brent settled below $80. Since the US attacked Iran in late February, Treasury yields had repeatedly moved with oil as disruptions to Hormuz altered the expected path of headline inflation, production costs and central-bank policy.

The latest proposal focused on reopening the strait rather than resolving the full US-Iran conflict. Qatar said an interim plan had been circulated, and both Bessent and Qatari representatives expressed hope that an agreement was close. Diplomats said Tehran had privately softened its opposition to European participation in demining, which could give shipowners and insurers an independent measure of whether the channel was safe.

Important conditions remained. A European naval operation would require Iranian security guarantees, a ceasefire that could hold and the assent of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, which has led attacks on shipping and whose members remained divided over foreign involvement. Iran continued to demand authority over the strait and the collection of transit fees, while the US opposed that arrangement. Talks with Oman centered on a new shipping channel believed to contain mines, so an agreement to negotiate would still have to be followed by physical clearance and a credible security framework.

Those limitations mattered because Tuesday’s market move reflected a lower probability of renewed disruption, not restored traffic. Observable transit had remained only a trickle, and five months of conflict had left import-dependent economies exposed to fuel and power shortages. The market nevertheless treated the change in Iran’s stance as more consequential than another general expression of interest in talks: outside participation in demining would address one of the practical obstacles preventing commercial shipping from returning.

The rates response was broad but strongest in the belly and at 10 years. The 5-year and 10-year yields each fell more than 6 basis points, compared with 4.5 basis points at 2 years and 5.3 basis points at 30 years. That pattern produced a modest flattening rather than a renewed bull steepening. It was consistent with investors removing some medium-term inflation and policy restraint while leaving a substantial long-end premium for fiscal supply and the possibility that the energy shock has lasting effects.

The breakeven decline accounted for slightly more than half of the 10-year nominal move. At 2.228%, the 10-year breakeven was 3.5 basis points lower on the day and 1.1 basis points lower over one month. The 10-year real yield, by contrast, remained 14.1 basis points above its level a month earlier despite Tuesday’s decline. Energy relief had therefore reversed the recent rise in inflation compensation more fully than the increase in the real discount rate.

Treasury activity increased as the rally developed. FINRA recorded $1.166 trillion of par trading, 5.4% more than the previous session, across 388,074 trades. Nominal-coupon activity rose 8.2% to $925 billion. Trading in coupons longer than 7 years through 10 years increased 15.9% to $165.6 billion, while activity in the greater-than-3-year through 5-year sector rose 10.4% to $239 billion. The figures do not identify investor direction, but they show that the largest yield declines occurred alongside increased cash-market participation rather than unusually light turnover.

Long-duration bond indices recovered more than the front end. The ICE US Government 20-plus-year index gained 0.78%, and the 7-to-10-year index rose 0.46%, compared with a 0.11% increase in the 1-to-3-year gauge. Even after the daily advance, the 20-plus-year index remained 2.81% lower over one month. The performance echoed the yield curve: falling crude produced meaningful relief, but it did not erase the accumulated cost of higher real yields and duration risk.

Risk assets treated the oil move as relief from a supply shock. The semiconductor index’s 6.55% gain led a technology rally, while the broader S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average reached records. Investment-grade and high-yield bond funds also advanced, with LQD up 0.61% and HYG up 0.30%. The dollar index slipped 0.09%. Gold futures rose 2.33% to $4,127.80, showing that demand for an inflation or geopolitical hedge persisted even as the immediate energy premium receded.

## Paulson Keeps the Inflation Test Ahead of the Fed

Paulson provided the day’s clearest new description of the policy choice confronting the Fed. The Philadelphia Fed president, who votes on monetary policy this year, said last week’s decision to leave rates unchanged was not close for her. She judged the current stance mildly restrictive, but framed that judgment as provisional rather than an argument for an extended hold.

Her first scenario is that improving inflation readings and stable expectations confirm that existing rates can return inflation to 2% within an acceptable period. The competing scenario is that the modest decline in underlying inflation over the past year shows policy is not restrictive enough. In that case, the passage of time without further progress would become evidence for tighter policy rather than a reason to continue waiting.

The distinction is important because Paulson estimates underlying inflation at 2.4% to 2.8%, still above the Fed’s target. She welcomed June’s improvement in the personal consumption expenditures price index but described it as only one step. Her condition for patience is continued progress in the measures beneath volatile food and energy prices, not merely another decline in crude. She also identified stable labor conditions, Middle East-driven price uncertainty and AI infrastructure investment as forces that could keep demand and selected prices firm.

June job openings offered limited relief. Available positions declined to 7.36 million from 7.54 million in May, more than expected, with pullbacks in health care, leisure and hospitality, wholesale trade and business services. Vacancies increased in transportation and warehousing, while federal-government postings reached their highest since late 2024. Hiring picked up slightly and dismissals were little changed. The release therefore showed some cooling in vacancies but not a broad deterioration in employment flows.

The US trade report added evidence of slower cross-border demand without establishing a domestic downturn. The goods-and-services deficit narrowed 5.6% in June to $73.3 billion. Imports fell 1.8%, their first decline since the start of the year, while exports decreased 0.9%. Trade had been volatile through the quarter as tariffs, the Iran conflict and AI-related investment altered the timing and composition of purchases.

Short-rate markets responded more to the fall in oil than to an abrupt change in the labor outlook. Futures priced about 15 basis points of tightening for the September meeting, more than half of a quarter-point increase, with one full move priced by year-end. As recently as the prior week, two increases had been fully reflected. Lower energy prices reduced the urgency for consecutive action, while Paulson’s conditions and the still-stable labor picture kept a single increase in the distribution.

The Treasury curve supported that interpretation. The 2-year yield reached its lowest level since July 20, but its 4.5-basis-point decline was smaller than the fall at 5 and 10 years. If investors had concluded that labor demand was breaking sharply, the front end would ordinarily have carried more of the rally. Instead, the market reduced the expected scale of tightening and removed inflation compensation through intermediate maturities while preserving the possibility that the Fed still acts later in the year.

Supply remained a separate restraint. Treasury is due to announce its August-to-October note and bond auction plans at 8:30 a.m. in Washington on Aug. 5. Since May 2024, officials have said nominal coupon and floating-rate-note auction sizes are likely to remain unchanged for at least the next several quarters. Dealers broadly expect that stance to survive the coming announcement, even though maturing debt and persistent deficits are likely to require larger fixed-rate borrowing programs next year.

The timing of the eventual increase is contested. The most common dealer estimate has moved to May 2027 from February, and some forecasts point to August. CIBC, Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo expect Treasury at least to soften the wording by removing “at least,” while JPMorgan strategists judge that such a change would be sensible but may be avoided because it could lift long-term yields. The distinction is between keeping current auction sizes stable and preparing investors for the point at which stability ends.

Tuesday’s rally therefore reduced the energy component of the policy and supply premium without resolving either issue. Oil can change the near-term inflation distribution quickly, but Paulson’s decision rule rests on underlying inflation, and the 30-year sector still faces a borrowing outlook that extends beyond the current diplomatic episode. That is why the long bond rallied yet remained above 5.17%, with a much larger monthly increase than the 2-year note.

## Primary Credit Rewards Clean Execution and Rejects Weak Terms

The US investment-grade primary market showed substantial demand for acquisition financing that was not tied to the AI borrowing cycle. AbbVie sold $10 billion of bonds to help finance its pending purchase of Apogee Therapeutics, attracting about $63 billion of peak orders. That was slightly more demand than Amazon received for a $25 billion sale the previous month and well above the approximately $39 billion of peak orders for AbbVie’s $8 billion issuance in February.

AbbVie had initially sought at least $8 billion. The completed nine-part transaction spanned maturities from 2 to 40 years. The longest bond priced to yield 92 basis points over Treasuries, about 33 basis points tighter than initial discussions, demonstrating that investors were willing to extend duration when the issuer, use of proceeds and transaction structure were readily identifiable.

The bonds will help fund AbbVie’s proposed $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee, expected to close during the current quarter. The purchase is intended to strengthen AbbVie’s anti-inflammatory drug portfolio as competition increases for Skyrizi. The company had also reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter results, supported by immunology, neuroscience and a recovery in Botox.

AbbVie was one of six investment-grade borrowers that raised a combined $17.3 billion on Tuesday, including acquisition financing for Skyworks Solutions. The reception distinguished conventional corporate funding from the recent fatigue surrounding data-center and AI debt. A $25 billion Amazon sale had been followed by weakness in AI-related bonds, and a July data-center financing involving BlackRock encountered soft initial demand. AbbVie’s much smaller borrowing need and non-AI acquisition rationale drew a deeper orderbook relative to deal size.

The leveraged-loan market supplied the opposite result. Baker Tilly abandoned a roughly $3 billion loan that would have refinanced private-credit debt and financed a dividend. Some prospective buyers demanded wider spreads than the accounting firm and its owners, Hellman & Friedman and Valeas Capital Partners, were prepared to offer. Baker Tilly said it had evaluated an opportunistic refinancing and could return when conditions were more favorable.

The proposed dividend could have reached $1 billion, which would have made it the largest non-investment-grade dividend transaction of the year. That use of proceeds weakened the bargain for creditors already assessing higher-for-longer rates and a heavy maturity calendar among lower-rated companies. The withdrawal showed that available liquidity did not eliminate investor resistance to transactions combining refinancing with a large sponsor payout.

The contrast was not simply between investment grade and leveraged finance. It reflected how investors differentiated borrowers and structures within a market still capable of absorbing large transactions. AbbVie increased its deal from the minimum contemplated size and tightened pricing substantially. Baker Tilly could not complete a similarly large refinancing when lenders sought more compensation for leverage and dividend extraction.

Secondary-market research pointed to a broader erosion at the boundary between high grade and junk. About $100 billion of bonds in US dollar and euro investment-grade indices were trading at spreads wider than the double-B curve. Oracle and Stellantis were among the large issuers whose debt had approached junk-market pricing, while an ICE BofA index of companies already downgraded from investment grade had risen to its highest since the start of 2024.

The pressure came from several directions. Oracle’s data-center spending made it a focus of concern about debt-funded AI investment, although its spreads had tightened back below double-B levels by the start of August after breaching them in July. Stellantis faced Chinese competition and a sharp decline in its equity value. Business-development companies and private-credit firms were also under scrutiny because of their exposure to software companies vulnerable to AI disruption.

Trading at a junk-like spread does not ensure a downgrade. Markets often reprice faster than rating agencies, and spreads can recover before the ratings change. Fitch said its analysis emphasizes revenue growth, margins, cash-flow generation and forward leverage through the cycle. The unusually large volume of investment-grade bonds that had recently crossed the double-B curve nevertheless showed that higher financing costs and technological disruption were no longer confined to clearly speculative borrowers.

That backdrop made Tuesday’s primary-market outcomes more informative. Credit remained open, but execution depended increasingly on whether investors were being compensated for the specific use of proceeds and deterioration risk. A highly rated pharmaceutical borrower financing an announced acquisition could attract orders equal to more than six times the deal size. A sponsor-owned company seeking both refinancing and a dividend could not clear at its preferred spread.

## Global Policy Divergence Meets an Energy-Led Growth Shock

The search for sovereign duration was shifting toward Europe as investors compared policy credibility, fiscal risk and inflation exposure across the US, UK and Japan. UBS Asset Management and Guinness Global Investors had been buying German bonds, Barings reduced Treasuries to add Italy, Spain and France, and Aviva Investors viewed euro-area positions as attractive. The common argument was that Europe’s weaker growth and more predictable monetary framework offered relative stability even after the Iran conflict lifted energy costs.

Pricing still contained a substantial amount of ECB tightening. Swaps implied a quarter-point increase during the year and a probability above 60% of another move, while a Euribor options trade targeted only 12.5 basis points of tightening by year-end against about 41 basis points embedded in swaps. The disagreement was not whether the energy shock mattered, but whether markets had priced too much persistence after German 10-year yields moved above 3%.

Europe’s attraction was qualified by internal fiscal differences. Investors remained wary of longer-dated Italian debt before September budget negotiations and political strains in Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s coalition. French 10-year bonds offered nearly 80 basis points more yield than German debt, creating a different balance between spread compensation and political risk. In Britain, attention remained fixed on the Oct. 28 budget and the financing of military investment and adult social care, with 30-year gilt yields already the highest among developed markets.

Japan presented a less settled combination of monetary and market pressure. Its 10-year government-bond auction drew the weakest demand since May 2025 as yields remained near multi-decade highs. The yen slipped 0.3% to about 157.70 per dollar, giving back part of the gain produced by joint US-Japan intervention. The currency remained weaker than the 155 level that strategists identified as an important test of whether the official action could generate a durable break from depreciation.

Japan had alternatives to selling Treasuries if further intervention required dollars. Citigroup identified the Fed’s Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility, roughly $160 billion of deposits at foreign central banks and euro assets as possible funding sources. Japan has more than $1.1 trillion of Treasuries, and Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said the country would use the Fed facility in the future. Those options reduce the immediate risk that currency defense automatically produces Treasury liquidation, although they do not solve the interest-rate gap behind the yen’s weakness.

After the US fixed-income close, Japanese wage data strengthened the case for another BOJ increase in coming months. Nominal wages rose 3.4% in June from a year earlier after a revised 3.3% gain in May, extending the run of increases above 3% to five months, the longest in 34 years. Base pay also rose 3.4%, while a measure for full-time workers excluding bonuses, overtime and sampling distortions increased 2.9%. Real wages gained 1.7% for a sixth consecutive month.

The figures followed six quarters of year-on-year gains in corporate profits and annual wage settlements above 5% for a third year among workers represented by Rengo. They supported the BOJ’s view that a tight labor market can sustain wage growth, even as food inflation and living costs continue to pressure households. The release occurred too late to explain Tuesday’s Treasury close, but it added to the policy divergence facing Asian trading: the US market had reduced expected tightening as oil fell, while Japanese domestic data reinforced the possibility of an earlier BOJ move.

Other central banks were still responding to the accumulated energy shock. Madagascar raised its policy rate to 12.5% from 12%, its first increase in more than a year, after concluding that conditions were no longer restrictive enough. The central bank lifted its year-end inflation forecast to 10.1% from 9.3% and said the move was intended to contain the projected rise in prices and anchor expectations toward its 5% medium-term target.

Across developing Asia, the damage extended beyond inflation readings. The Asian Development Bank lowered its 2026 growth forecast for developing Asia and the Pacific to 4.9% from 5.1% and raised its inflation projection to 4.3% from 3.6%. Satellite observations showed nighttime light diminishing across nearly 60% of the region’s land area since the conflict began, with import-dependent Bangladesh, Pakistan and Cambodia among the most affected. Fuel shortages and costs had disrupted manufacturing, transport and tourism, while the ADB warned that debt accumulation, job cuts and lower investment could persist after oil prices retreat.

Europe faced a different supply constraint. The Rhine’s water level at Kaub fell to 21 centimeters, the lowest on record, and was forecast to decline to 17 centimeters by Saturday. Barges were reducing loads, freight costs were rising and low water was restricting some French nuclear generation. One estimate put the possible drag on German growth at 0.3 percentage point for the year. The development complicated the notion that Europe’s inflation outlook was uniformly benign: weaker activity supports bonds, but transport and power disruptions can also raise near-term costs.

ECB research found that euro-area households reduced discretionary spending after the Iran war primarily because of uncertainty rather than budget constraints alone. Nominal energy spending rose, while housing and food expenditure remained resilient and higher-income households made the largest reductions. That pattern suggested a sentiment channel capable of weakening demand even before the full increase in energy costs reached household balance sheets.

## Forward Market Significance

The Aug. 5 Treasury refunding announcement is the most immediate US duration event. Coupon auction sizes are broadly expected to remain unchanged for the August-to-October quarter. The market-sensitive question is whether officials retain the commitment to stable nominal coupon and floating-rate-note sizes for “at least” several more quarters or soften the wording to prepare investors for increases in 2027. Removing that phrase would not enlarge the current auctions, but it could bring the supply transition closer in long-end pricing.

The Reserve Bank of India also decides on Aug. 5. Twenty-nine of 30 surveyed economists expect the repo rate to remain at 5.25%, with one forecasting a quarter-point increase. Inflation accelerated to 4.38% in June, above the RBI’s 4% target for the first time in 17 months, while the finance ministry warned that price pressure was broadening beyond food. Most economists expect the RBI to retain its 5.1% fiscal-year inflation forecast and 6.6% growth projection, though lower recent oil prices give it scope to revise inflation down.

Governor Sanjay Malhotra’s conditions for a future increase will matter more than the widely anticipated hold. Interest-rate swaps imply 75 to 100 basis points of tightening, with most of it shifted into next year, while many economists expect increases to begin in October. More than $40 billion of capital has entered India since authorities eased rules for foreign-currency deposits and overseas borrowing, supporting liquidity and the rupee. The RBI must decide how much of those inflows to absorb into reserves while judging whether energy costs are spreading into consumer prices.

Friday’s US employment report will determine whether the decline in openings represents meaningful labor cooling. The current expectation is for payrolls to rise by 85,000 after a 57,000 gain in June, with unemployment at 4.2%. A stronger outcome would support Paulson’s concern that mildly restrictive policy may not be sufficient if underlying inflation stalls. A weaker report would reinforce the reduction in expected Fed tightening, particularly if crude remains near Tuesday’s lower levels.

Hormuz remains the faster-moving test. A drafted proposal and Iran’s willingness to consider European demining lowered oil prices before ships had resumed normal passage. The next evidence must come from a durable ceasefire, Iranian security assurances, IRGC consent and actual mine-clearing access. Agreement on those steps would reduce the probability that energy again lifts breakevens and forces earlier tightening. Disagreement over control, transit fees or foreign naval participation would expose how much of the two-day bond rally depended on an arrangement that was still incomplete.

Japan’s wage report shifts the Asian policy focus toward the timing of the BOJ’s next move. Sustained nominal pay growth above 3%, six months of real-wage gains and firm corporate profits strengthen the case for an increase by December and leave September in consideration. Whether the yen can hold away from its recent lows without another intervention will determine how much urgency policymakers attach to that option. Renewed depreciation would test both Japan’s funding choices and the US effort to prevent currency defense from spilling into Treasury sales.

Credit investors will continue to distinguish market access from acceptable terms. AbbVie’s $63 billion orderbook showed that a large acquisition financing could clear with substantial price tightening, while Baker Tilly’s withdrawal showed the limit of demand for a leveraged refinancing tied to a sponsor dividend. The next transactions will reveal whether that divide remains issuer-specific or becomes a broader constraint as the potential fallen-angel universe and the calendar of leveraged maturities expand.

section_summaries.summary: European sovereign debt attracted relative demand as investors weighed weaker growth and steadier policy against fiscal and energy risks, while Japan’s weak bond auction and renewed yen depreciation exposed a less settled policy mix. Across developing Asia, the energy shock lowered the regional growth forecast and raised expected inflation, while record-low Rhine water threatened European transport, power supply and German activity.

The immediate tests are Treasury’s Aug. 5 refunding language, Friday’s US employment report and whether Hormuz diplomacy produces enforceable security and mine-clearing steps. Together they will show whether the rally can progress beyond lower oil risk or remains vulnerable to renewed supply, inflation and Fed pressure.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries extend rally as Hormuz diplomacy drives oil and inflation expectations lower
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries advanced for a second session as signs of progress toward an interim Hormuz arrangement pushed WTI down 6.41% to $75.19 and Brent down 5.96% to $78.78. The 2-year yield fell 4.5 basis points to 4.193%, the 5-year declined 6.2 basis points to 4.326%, the 10-year dropped 6.3 basis points to 4.615% and the 30-year eased 5.3 basis points to 5.176%.

The rally reflected both less inflation compensation and lower real rates: the 10-year breakeven fell 3.5 basis points to 2.228%, while the 10-year real yield declined 2.8 basis points to 2.387%. Investors reduced expected Fed tightening as energy risk receded, but strong equities, only moderate labor cooling and Anna Paulson’s warning about stalled underlying inflation kept one increase priced by year-end.

Relief remained conditional because normal shipping had not resumed and a durable ceasefire, Iranian security assurances, IRGC consent and mine-clearing access were unresolved. Longer yields also remained above month-earlier levels, preserving a supply and inflation premium beyond the immediate diplomatic episode. Credit markets reinforced the importance of terms: AbbVie drew heavy demand for acquisition financing, while Baker Tilly withdrew a leveraged refinancing tied to a large sponsor dividend.
